version_guard.provenance: This pin predates the version-straddle guard (scripts/probe-version-guard.sh, added 2026-09-26 by claudepr-9fe76ef4), so it carries no start/end bracket of its own; its single-version provenance is the documented 2026-09-24 discipline instead: the host auto-updated 2.1.281 -> 2.1.282 mid-re-pin, the straddled first run was discarded in full, and the whole suite was re-run to completion against 2.1.282 before this fixture was written (docs/notes/claude-contract-probes.md, Re-measurement history). Every later re-pin records the guard verdicts here instead: start and end from each probe's 'version-guard: verdict=single-version' line, with start == end == claude_version across all four probes (enforced by tests/probe_version_guard.rs).

notes.isolation: Every probe ran with HOME redirected into a throwaway sandbox; the host's real ~/.claude files were never read or written. Auth traveled by inherited environment only.
notes.cross_source_order_evidence: 2.1.282 run: P2's SessionStart pair fired relay-first (relay ...292.005941 vs project ...292.008763, ~2.8 ms apart) while its Stop pair fired project-first (~3 ms apart) - the flip visible without any sleeping-hook experiment, confirming again that only the merge (all loaded sources fire) is contractual. P6: user Stop ...320.628 vs relay Stop ...320.632. The dedicated sleeping-hook probe (Arm S of scripts/probe-stop-edge-contracts.sh, re-measured 2026-09-25 against this same 2.1.282, claudepr-d9553d38): project hook sleeping 300 ms (measured wall 305-310 ms) vs relay hook 0 ms - the two hooks ran concurrently in 12/12 event pairs and the relay started before the project hook in 6/12 (2.3-6.0 ms ahead; two earlier same-day invocations of the same probe: 4/12 and 5/12 flips, concurrent 12/12 each). Concurrency, not ordering, is the guarantee.
notes.tui_per_turn_evidence: Two turns in one TUI session (probe-tui-second-turn.sh): turn 1 fired 1 Stop with reply rendered (41.6 s), turn 2 fired 1 Stop with reply rendered SECOND-OK (3.3 s); TUI screen showed (running stop hook) on both. The tool-using arms matched: probe-1 T2 fired 1 Stop per loaded source per turn (2 firings per turn across user+project, 62.5 s / 32.5 s) and Arm T's multi-round prompt fired exactly 1 Stop (60.5 s). Arm T's second prompt that evening was an incomplete turn (no reply, no Stop after a 205 s wait) - per the maintenance doc an incomplete turn is a re-run, not a contract finding; the same arm completed cleanly on 2.1.281 earlier the same day (1 Stop, 60.0 s).
notes.degraded_path_hazard: Historical (2.1.270): on runs where the model's tool calls are permission-DENIED (no allowlist, headless), one run out of two produced an extra Stop firing. Re-measured against this same 2.1.282 on 2026-09-25 (claudepr-d9553d38, scripts/probe-stop-edge-contracts.sh Arm D): 15 completed denied runs across three invocations - all exit 0, stop_hook_active false, the model's own reply confirming its Bash calls were blocked - and every run fired exactly one Stop; the hazard did not reproduce. Kept on record as historical (mechanism unexplained, small samples; not reachable in the NEEDLE fleet - claude-print.yaml passes --dangerously-skip-permissions). The single-fire poller keeps its tolerance: first payload -> transcript retry/fallback, watchdog bounds the session.
notes.print_mode_tool_use_evidence: Two sequential permitted Bash rounds in one -p run (Arm P): exactly 1 Stop at the turn's true end (payload last_assistant_message: DONE, stop_hook_active: false, single session id), claude exit 0. The unallowlisted T1 arm also completed this time (exit 0) with exactly 1 Stop of its own.
notes.cutoff_evidence: A -p run cut off by --max-turns fires no Stop of its own: T3 (--max-turns 2, exit 1) added zero firings on 2.1.282, exactly as on 2.1.281 (where the T1 arm outgrowing --max-turns 6 showed the same shape) and 2.1.270 - cutoffs belong to the --stop-hook-timeout watchdog, not the Stop poller.
notes.hook_timeout_evidence: Arm T (added 2026-09-26, claudepr-352cf1df, scripts/probe-stop-edge-contracts.sh): the relay-position hook (--settings file, run with --setting-sources= so it is the only loaded hook - the isolation-mode shape) configured with a per-hook timeout of 5 s while sleeping 30 s, wired on SessionStart and Stop. Two invocations of 4 single-turn runs each against this same pinned 2.1.282 (a full three-arm run, then an Arm-T-only run ARM_S_RUNS=0 ARM_D_RUNS=0; the host binary had drifted to 2.1.283, so the persisted versions-dir 2.1.282 was measured on a PATH shim - the probe stamped the version itself): all 16 event firings KILLED (start logged, end never - the 30 s sleep never completed), every run exit 0 with the reply rendered (reply-contains-OK 4/4 per invocation), and the claude process exiting 5.0 s after the Stop hook's start in 8/8 runs - the configured timeout, not the 30 s sleep. Enforcement is of the per-hook timeout field itself (measured at 5 s), which is the same field src/hook.rs sets to 10 on both relay hooks - the measured form of hook-design.md's 'does not wait beyond the 10s timeout' clause.
